paths.title: Threat Modeling
paths.description: Identify assets, trust boundaries, attack paths, and proportionate controls before implementation.
concept: A threat model explains what must be protected, from whom, across which boundaries, and with what consequences.
Controls are effective only when they address realistic attack paths and protect important assets.
workflow: Create a practical threat model
Model one concrete system flow at a time.
Keep the model connected to design decisions and update it as architecture changes.
Identify users, services, data, and secrets.
Draw data flows and trust boundaries.
List entry points and privileged operations.
Describe plausible attacker goals.
Rank threats by impact and feasibility.
Assign preventive and detective controls.
Record residual risk and owners.
question: Locate a trust boundary
Which transition most clearly crosses a trust boundary?
A local function calling another local function
Untrusted browser input entering an authenticated server endpoint
A variable being renamed
A comment being edited
Data moves from a client-controlled environment into a trusted service that must validate identity, authorization, and input.
checklist: Confirm that the model results in actionable engineering work.
A diagram without decisions, owners, and validation does not reduce risk.

paths.title: Identity and Access Control
paths.description: Implement authentication, session security, least privilege, and object-level authorization.
concept: Authorization belongs at every protected object boundary
A valid session does not imply permission to read or modify every resource.
Broken object-level authorization occurs when a server trusts a client identifier without verifying access.
workflow: Authorize a protected request
Make the decision from trusted identity and server-owned policy.
Authorization checks should be consistent across APIs, jobs, and administrative tools.
Authenticate the request and validate the session.
Load the target resource.
Determine the required action.
Evaluate role, ownership, tenant, and policy rules.
Deny by default.
Record sensitive decisions safely.
Test same-role and cross-tenant attacks.
question: Apply least privilege
A reporting service only reads aggregated data. Which permission is appropriate?
Database administrator
Read-only access to required views
Permission to drop every table
Shared root credentials
The service should receive only the minimum data and operations required for its function.
checklist: Confirm that accounts and sessions cannot silently gain excessive power.
Identity controls must include recovery, revocation, and monitoring, not only sign-in.
Passwords use a modern salted hash.
Sessions expire and can be revoked.
Sensitive actions require recent authentication where appropriate.

paths.title: Detection and Incident Response
paths.description: Prepare telemetry, triage, containment, evidence preservation, recovery, and learning.
concept: Incident response is a prepared capability
Teams respond faster when roles, evidence sources, containment options, and communication paths are defined in advance.
The goal is to restore service, understand scope, preserve evidence, and prevent recurrence.
workflow: Handle a suspected compromise
Use a controlled sequence that protects evidence and limits further harm.
Actions should be recorded with timestamps and decision owners.
Validate the alert and assign severity.
Preserve relevant logs and volatile evidence.
Identify affected identities, hosts, and data.
Contain access without destroying evidence.
Remove persistence and close the exploited path.
Restore from trusted state.
Monitor for recurrence.
Run a lessons review.
question: Choose the first response priority
A credential is confirmed stolen and actively used. What is the immediate priority?
Redesign the website colors
Contain access by revoking or rotating the credential
Delete every log
Wait for another incident
Active unauthorized access must be contained while preserving evidence needed to determine scope.
checklist: Verify that the organization can detect, contain, and communicate an incident.
Exercises reveal missing access, unclear authority, and unavailable evidence before a real event.
Severity levels and escalation paths are defined.
Critical logs are retained and time-synchronized.
Legal and communication contacts are known.
